Hi Neha,

MedTech's compliance team has one outstanding item before we sign the DPA amendment: our cleanroom ingest pipeline produces a set of ephemeral logs and backups that include pseudonymized telemetry. The auditors ask for clarity on the following points so we can document them in the SOC evidence package:

- Where backups of cleanroom data are stored (object store, region, subprocessor).
- Retention windows for backups vs. primary indices (policy + automatic purge cadence).
- Deletion workflow for emergency erasures and how it impacts cold snapshots.
- Any exceptions (e.g., forensic hold) and the expected timeline to lift holds.

I attached a short list of MedTech requirements (medtech-retention-ask.pdf) to show the fields they need populated. Could you (a) confirm whether Redwood keeps separate backup lanes for cleanroom data, and (b) provide a proposed purge timeline we can reference in the amendment?

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by the details below and two attachments (redwood-cleanroom-playbook.pdf and backup-retention-matrix.csv):

- Backups: Cleanroom backups are written to a logically separated bucket with server-side encryption (AES-256) in the primary region you selected (us-west-2). The storage is managed by our cloud subprocessor (FastStore Inc.).
- Retention/purge cadence: Primary indices: 30 days default. Cold snapshots/backups: 90 days default, with an optional 180-day tier for enterprise accounts. We can scope a 60-day compromise for cleanroom-only buckets if that helps your compliance posture.
- Deletion workflow: Normal deletions are initiated via our orchestration API and execute a coordinated cascade: delete primary -> mark associated backup snapshots for tombstone -> background purge job removes snapshots within the configured window. Emergency erasures trigger an expedited purge request that flags the object for immediate deletion and an expedited subprocessor removal request (target SLA 72 hours to remove from accessible buckets, longer for immutable offsite archival depending on subprocessor).
- Forensic/legal holds: We support legal holds; lifting a hold requires written consent from your legal team. Holds prevent automated purge jobs; once lifted we resume the normal purge cadence and provide you a signed hold-release timeline.

Notes and caveats:
- FastStore's replication to DR region is governed by their subprocessor agreement; we can request a subprocessor-specific deletion confirmation but cannot directly control their internal retention beyond our contract.
- If you need guaranteed physical overwriting (air-gapped deletion), that's considered an Exception and will be scoped as a paid professional-services engagement.

I'll attach the retention matrix for clarity. Marissa — can you pick up the DocuSign/contract language items if Julia's team wants to capture the 60-day cleanroom window?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Adding a couple of operational details from infra so your auditors have concrete answers. Also attaching current subprocessors list (subprocessors-current.csv).

- Subprocessor: FastStore Inc. (object storage). Backups are kept in a dedicated cleanroom bucket with ACLs restricted to the backup service account; network egress restricted through VPC endpoints.
- Cold snapshots: Ingest snapshots are exported nightly and retained as immutable objects for the configured snapshot window. We tag snapshots with the dataset-id + requestor and retain that metadata for 90 days by default.
- Emergency erasure flow: When marked emergency, the snapshot object is marked tombstoned, an expedited deletion ticket is opened with FastStore, and we mark the related Dynamo/Index shards for immediate compaction. We aim for visibility that deletion has occurred within 72 hours; however FastStore's internal garbage collection can add up to an additional 7 days before physical object cleanup in DR replicas. We will send you a deletion confirmation (screenshot/log) once we have FastStore's ack.

Julia — let us know if your auditors need the exact S3 key naming pattern or sample logs; we can redact and provide a sample artifact.

Karthik
